rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.

No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: [OWNERSHIP_PATH] MainShape > hasPropulsionLoadCase > node > shaftLineLoadCaseType > or[1]: The blade-failure branch places bladeFailureUltimateLoad and combinedAxialBendingTorsionLoad property constraints inside a shape applied to the shaftLineLoadCaseType value, rather than to the loadCase node that owns those properties. Consequently, valid blade-failure load cases will not be checked for the required load inputs, while the controlled type value is incorrectly required to own them. Required change: Restructure the conditional so the blade-failure test is applied to the loadCase node and its load-input property constraints are evaluated on that same loadCase node; retain the extreme-operational and fatigue alternatives on shaftLineLoadCaseType. | [DATATYPE_QUANTITY_ACCESS] MainShape > sh:sparql > bendingYieldSafetyFactor and torsionalYieldSafetyFactor checks: The direct checks only require matching qudt:numericValue and qudt:unit triples. They do not require each safety-factor value to be a qudt:QuantityValue with exactly one decimal numeric value and exactly one unitless unit, despite the canonical terms having QuantityValue range and dimensionless quantity semantics. A factor node with multiple values or units, or without the required quantity type, can therefore pass. Required change: Constrain each safety-factor node as a qudt:QuantityValue with exactly one xsd:decimal qudt:numericValue and exactly one qudt:unit equal to qudt:UNITLESS, while retaining the exact-one-factor and minimum-1.0 checks.

[LOGIC] MainShape > hasPropulsionLoadCase > sh:node > sh:or: The blade-failure branch uses sh:or among the load-case type, blade-failure ultimate load, and combined axial-bending-torsion load property shapes. Consequently, a blade-failure load case can pass with only its type and no required load inputs, while a load case can also pass without the required blade-failure applicability by providing only one operand or an extreme-operational/fatigue type. Required change: Require the bladeFailureLoadCase type together with both bladeFailureUltimateLoad and combinedAxialBendingTorsionLoad inputs, and do not let the alternative property shapes independently satisfy the requirement; preserve the conditional safety-factor check for the applicable blade-failure case.
